criteria.criterion: AC1 — A review-plan run in which one or more LLM step calls fail but the run still produces a verdict carries coverage.llm_step_failures in the emitted JSON, shaped {"total": <int>, "by_step": {<call label>: <int>}}
AC2 — A run with NO failed LLM step calls does not carry the key at all: coverage is byte-identical to the pre-change output
AC3 — The count never alters the verdict string, the exit code, the signature, or the provenance stamp; failure classification and swallow behaviour of every existing site is unchanged
AC4 — The sink is run-scoped and does not leak: record outside an active scope is a no-op that never raises, the scope is dropped on exit, and a second run in the same process starts from zero

AC5 — coverage.llm_step_failures is declared and described in src/rebar/schemas/plan_review_verdict.schema.json, and the human-readable review-plan text output prints one line naming the total and the per-step counts when the key is present
AC6 — by_step keys use the runner's _call_label verbatim, so a key matches the 'llm call [<label>] ... FAILED' log line

AC7 — Held-out unit tests cover: record→drain round-trip with multiple labels; no-failure run omits the key; record outside a scope is a silent no-op; drain is destructive so a second run starts at zero; and the verdict-assembly site adds the key only when non-empty

AC8 — One wiring test closes the gap between the unit tests and AC1's end-to-end claim: with the sink scope active, a runner call driven to failure is recorded under the expected label and reaches coverage.llm_step_failures through the same drain
